subject: How to fill the area below a line with the line color?

messages.author: 7c598f9d5aed052f
messages.subject: How to fill the area below a line with the line color?
parts:
The data I have are in the dput() output at the end of this mail; an easier way to look at them is

> cast( melt( x, c( "Limit", "Tty" ), "down" ), Limit ~ Tty )
Limit fo qs ret sp1 sp2
1 0 NA 100 50 NA NA
2 200 NA 100 50 100 NA
3 1000 NA 20 10 100 100
4 2000 100 10 5 50 100
5 2500 100 8 4 40 80

I get a nice line graph which is almost exactly what I'm looking for with

> q <- ggplot( data = x, aes( x = Limit, y = down, color = Tty ) )
> q <- q + geom_line( size = 1 )

I would be so grateful if I knew how to fill the area below each line, down to the next one, with the line colour. I went through the documentation, looked at a thread in the mailing list from Feb 2010, played around with geom_area(), saw a lot of stacked colourful graphs but nothing near to me real goal.

Would somebody have a hint for me?

Thanks,
Rainer


> dput(x)
structure(list(Limit = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 200L, 200L, 200L,
200L, 200L, 1000L, 1000L, 1000L, 1000L, 1000L, 2000L, 2000L,
2000L, 2000L, 2000L, 2500L, 2500L, 2500L, 2500L, 2500L), Tty = structure(c(3L,
2L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 3L, 2L,
4L, 5L, 1L, 3L, 2L, 4L, 5L, 1L), .Label = c("fo", "qs", "ret",
"sp1", "sp2"), class = "factor"), down = c(50L, 100L, NA, NA,
NA, 50L, 100L, 100L, NA, NA, 10L, 20L, 100L, 100L, NA, 5L, 10L,
50L, 100L, 100L, 4L, 8L, 40L, 80L, 100L)), .Names = c("Limit",
"Tty", "down"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -25L))

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: How to fill the area below a line with the line color?
parts:
Hi Rainer,

It is not a very elegant example of data manipulation, but it gets the
job done. By the way, thanks for providing data via dput(), very
nice!

## order levels from highest to lowest and sort
x$Tty <- factor(x$Tty, levels = c("fo", "sp2", "sp1", "qs", "ret"))
x <- x[order(x$Tty), ]

## use lagged down values
x$ymin <- c(x$down[-c(1:5)], rep(0, 5))

## now you can just use ribbons
ggplot(data = x, aes(x = Limit, fill = Tty)) +
geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ymin, ymax = down))


Cheers,

Josh

parts:
Thanks, Josh!

I had come a lettle closer to my desired outcome tinkering around with geom_polygon() but your solution is much better. After all, the very nature of the
data *is* a kind of ribbon!

My nowledge is very basic, but I try to understand problems in the mailing list, and sometimes I may even be able to help. I usually find it the most
frustrating part to get the data from a mail into R - that's why I use dput(). Should be done more regularly!

Thanks again,
Rainer
